rom_read_bandwidth_efficiency.note: Fraction of the ROM array's peak sweep rate sustained in practice. The study reports the underated ceiling alongside it because this derate moves the ROM answer directly.

designs.sizing_rule: smallest device count within 2% of the best per-user latency at batch 1, bounded at 4x the minimum feasible count. SRAM-KV designs are sized at batch 1 because SRAM is silicon area; HBM-KV designs are provisioned for batch 256 for both KV capacity and enough KV bandwidth to keep KV off the critical path ahead of the ROM sweep, capped by the die-edge beachfront a shipping GPU achieves

area_split_per_device.policy: balanced ROM+MAC: the array is grown into the spare silicon as replicated copies and the MAC array is sized to consume exactly what it can read, at one weight byte per multiply-accumulate

Taalas describes one transistor per 4-bit parameter doing both, so the multiplier is small but cannot be 1.0. This is the second most load-bearing assumption in this file after the ROM-to-SRAM cell ratio, and it decides the storage-versus-compute-in-ROM comparison.
rom_cell_area_multiplier.source: no published compute-in-ROM bitcell at any node

rom_full_array_sweep_time_s.note: rom_capacity_density_bytes_mm2 / (rom_read_bandwidth_density * rom_read_efficiency). time to read every stored weight once; independent of model size, batch and expert coverage, so it is a hard per-token ceiling for a ROM design. It is also independent of the CELL, because both densities carry the cell-area multiplier: a compute-in-ROM array and a storage-only array sweep in the same time and differ only in how much they hold

rom_read_bandwidth_efficiency.note: Fraction of the ROM array's peak sweep rate sustained in practice. rom_cell_area_multiplier.note: area of a compute-in-ROM cell relative to a storage-only mask-ROM cell. rom_read_bandwidth_efficiency.note: Fraction of the ROM array's peak sweep rate sustained in practice. A mask-ROM sweep is the most regular access pattern available -- a compile-time-fixed linear walk of the whole array with no arbitration, no conflicts and no refresh -- so 0.75 is a conservative charge and 0.90-1.00 is arguable. rom_full_array_sweep_time_s.note: rom_capacity_density_bytes_mm2 / (rom_read_bandwidth_density * rom_read_efficiency). time to read every stored weight once; independent of model size, batch and expert coverage, so it is a hard per-token ceiling for a ROM design. It is also independent of the CELL, because both densities carry the cell-area multiplier: a compute-in-ROM array and a storage-only array sweep in the same time and differ only in how much they hold
rom_full_array_sweep_time_s.source: https://semiwiki.com/semiconductor-manufacturers/tsmc/283487-tsmcs-5nm-0-021um2-sram-cell-using-euv-and-high-mobility-channel-with-write-assist-at-isscc2020/ ; no fabricated leading-node mask-ROM bitcell has been published for this program ; no published mask-ROM macro floorplan at a leading node ; no published compute-in-ROM bitcell at any node ; https://doi.org/10.1145/3489517.3530576 ; counting convention: one multiply plus one add is two operations ; https://en.wikichip.org/wiki/28_nm_lithography_process ; https://semiwiki.com/semiconductor-manufacturers/tsmc/283487-tsmcs-5nm-0-021um2-sram-cell-using-euv-and-high-mobility-channel-with-write-assist-at-isscc2020/ ; no published compute-in-ROM bitcell at any node ; no fabricated array to measure

rom_read_bandwidth_density_bytes_s_mm2.note: storage_rom_read_bytes_s_per_mm2 / cim_cell_area_multiplier. N5 compute-in-ROM array read-bandwidth density: a larger cell means fewer cells per mm2 and no extra bitlines or sense amps
rom_read_bandwidth_density_bytes_s_mm2.source: https://doi.org/10.1145/3489517.3530576 ; counting convention: one multiply plus one add is two operations ; https://en.wikichip.org/wiki/28_nm_lithography_process ; https://semiwiki.com/semiconductor-manufacturers/tsmc/283487-tsmcs-5nm-0-021um2-sram-cell-using-euv-and-high-mobility-channel-with-write-assist-at-isscc2020/ ; no published compute-in-ROM bitcell at any node

rom_read_bandwidth_efficiency.note: Fraction of the ROM array's peak sweep rate sustained in practice. A mask-ROM sweep is the most regular access pattern available -- a compile-time-fixed linear walk of the whole array with no arbitration, no conflicts and no refresh -- so 0.75 is a conservative charge and 0.90-1.00 is arguable. The study reports the underated ceiling alongside it because this derate moves the ROM answer directly.

sram_capacity_density_bits_mm2.note: 1e6 um2/mm2 / (bitcell_um2 / array_efficiency). N5 6T high-density SRAM array capacity density in bits/mm2
sram_capacity_density_bits_mm2.source: https://semiwiki.com/semiconductor-manufacturers/tsmc/283487-tsmcs-5nm-0-021um2-sram-cell-using-euv-and-high-mobility-channel-with-write-assist-at-isscc2020/ ; no vendor macro floorplan published for the target arrays

sram_read_bandwidth_density_bytes_s_mm2.note: (anchor_sram_read_bytes_s / anchor_die_area_mm2) * (anchor_bitcell_um2 / target_bitcell_um2). N5 SRAM array read-bandwidth density in bytes/s/mm2; the anchor rate is charged against WHOLE-die area and then applied only to array area, which is conservative

sram_read_bandwidth_efficiency.note: fraction of the SRAM array's peak read rate sustained by a real gather pattern

designs.sizing_rule: smallest device count within 2% of the best per-user latency at batch 1, bounded at 4x the minimum feasible count. SRAM-KV designs are sized at batch 1 because SRAM is silicon area; HBM-KV designs are provisioned for batch 256 for both KV capacity and enough KV bandwidth to keep KV off the critical path ahead of the ROM sweep, capped by the die-edge beachfront a shipping GPU achieves

A compute-in-ROM cell carries a pass transistor and the product-line wiring that lets it select one pre-computed partial product, on top of the via programming that stores its bits. Taalas describes one transistor per 4-bit parameter doing both, so the multiplier is small but cannot be 1.0. This is the second most load-bearing assumption in this file after the ROM-to-SRAM cell ratio, and it decides the storage-versus-compute-in-ROM comparison.

rom_read_bandwidth_efficiency.note: Fraction of the ROM array's peak sweep rate sustained in practice. A mask-ROM sweep is the most regular access pattern available -- a compile-time-fixed linear walk of the whole array with no arbitration, no conflicts and no refresh -- so 0.75 is a conservative charge and 0.90-1.00 is arguable. The study reports the underated ceiling alongside it because this derate moves the ROM answer directly.

sram_capacity_density_bits_mm2.source: https://semiwiki.com/semiconductor-manufacturers/tsmc/283487-tsmcs-5nm-0-021um2-sram-cell-using-euv-and-high-mobility-channel-with-write-assist-at-isscc2020/ ; no vendor macro floorplan published for the target arrays

N5 SRAM array read-bandwidth density in bytes/s/mm2; the anchor rate is charged against WHOLE-die area and then applied only to array area, which is conservative

sram_read_bandwidth_efficiency.note: fraction of the SRAM array's peak read rate sustained by a real gather pattern

designs.sizing_rule: smallest device count within 2% of the best per-user latency at batch 1, bounded at 4x the minimum feasible count. SRAM-KV designs are sized at batch 1 because SRAM is silicon area; HBM-KV designs are provisioned for batch 256 for both KV capacity and enough KV bandwidth to keep KV off the critical path ahead of the ROM sweep, capped by the die-edge beachfront a shipping GPU achieves

area_split_per_device.policy: balanced ROM+MAC: the array is grown into the spare silicon as replicated copies and the MAC array is sized to consume exactly what it can read, at one weight byte per multiply-accumulate

Taalas describes one transistor per 4-bit parameter doing both, so the multiplier is small but cannot be 1.0. This is the second most load-bearing assumption in this file after the ROM-to-SRAM cell ratio, and it decides the storage-versus-compute-in-ROM comparison.
rom_cell_area_multiplier.source: no published compute-in-ROM bitcell at any node

rom_full_array_sweep_time_s.note: rom_capacity_density_bytes_mm2 / (rom_read_bandwidth_density * rom_read_efficiency). time to read every stored weight once; independent of model size, batch and expert coverage, so it is a hard per-token ceiling for a ROM design. rom_read_bandwidth_efficiency.note: Fraction of the ROM array's peak sweep rate sustained in practice. A mask-ROM sweep is the most regular access pattern available -- a compile-time-fixed linear walk of the whole array with no arbitration, no conflicts and no refresh -- so 0.75 is a conservative charge and 0.90-1.00 is arguable. The study reports the underated ceiling alongside it because this derate moves the ROM answer directly.

rom_cell_area_multiplier.note: area of a compute-in-ROM cell relative to a storage-only mask-ROM cell. A compute-in-ROM cell carries a pass transistor and the product-line wiring that lets it select one pre-computed partial product, on top of the via programming that stores its bits. Taalas describes one transistor per 4-bit parameter doing both, so the multiplier is small but cannot be 1.0. This is the second most load-bearing assumption in this file after the ROM-to-SRAM cell ratio, and it decides the storage-versus-compute-in-ROM comparison.

It is also independent of the CELL, because both densities carry the cell-area multiplier: a compute-in-ROM array and a storage-only array sweep in the same time and differ only in how much they hold

rom_read_bandwidth.note: Fraction of the ROM array's peak sweep rate sustained in practice. A mask-ROM sweep is the most regular access pattern available -- a compile-time-fixed linear walk of the whole array with no arbitration, no conflicts and no refresh -- so 0.75 is a conservative charge and 0.90-1.00 is arguable. The study reports the underated ceiling alongside it because this derate moves the ROM answer directly.

stage_balance.note: penalty applied to a multi-device pipeline for imperfect layer balance across devices

stack_bandwidth_bytes_s.note: B200 SXM delivers 8 TB/s across eight HBM3E stacks: 8 TB/s / 8. Micron publishes over 1.2 TB/s per HBM3E stack at full pin speed (https://www.micron.com/products/memory/hbm/hbm3e), so 1.0 TB/s is the rate a shipping system actually clocks and is the conservative choice.

stack_beachfront_mm.note: 11 mm x 11 mm HBM3E package plus routing keep-out

stack_capacity_bytes.note: B200 SXM ships 180 GB across eight HBM3E stacks: 180 GB / 8. Micron's published HBM3E 12-high part is 36 GB per stack (https://www.micron.com/about/blog/applications/ai/micron-continues-memory-industry-leadership-with-hbm3e-12-high-36gb), so this is the SHIPPING-SYSTEM figure rather than the densest available die stack. Deriving it from the reference GPU keeps both sides of the iso-area comparison on identical memory technology, which is the point.

hop_latency_s.note: InfiniBand/Ethernet class scale-out hop. Not measured.

bytes_s.note: NVLink 4/5 class unidirectional payload rate per GPU, taken as half of the quoted 1.8 TB/s bidirectional

hop_latency_s.note: NVLink point-to-point sits around 1 us for small messages. A real all-reduce is two phases through a switch plus launch and synchronisation overhead, so 1.5 us is optimistic; 3-10 us is common in practice. Sweep upward, never downward.
300 ns per organic/silicon-interposer chiplet hop. Not measured.

bytes_s.note: Cerebras WSE-3 aggregate fabric bandwidth, 26.75 PB/s, used as the on-wafer payload-serialisation ceiling

hop_latency_s.note: 100 ns per on-wafer reticle-to-reticle hop; a stitched on-wafer link has no SerDes, no packet framing and no switch, so it is well under a package hop. Not measured.

technology_derivations.rom_sweep_note: The ROM full-array sweep time is rom_capacity_density divided by rom_read_bandwidth_density. Both scale with the same published bitcell-area ratio under this derivation, so the sweep time -- and hence the ROM path's hard per-token ceiling -- is the SAME at every node. Process scaling buys a ROM design capacity, not per-token speed. No clock-frequency bonus is credited, which makes this the conservative reading.

rom_cell_area_multiplier.note: area of a compute-in-ROM cell relative to a storage-only mask-ROM cell. A compute-in-ROM cell carries a pass transistor and the product-line wiring that lets it select one pre-computed partial product, on top of the via programming that stores its bits. Taalas describes one transistor per 4-bit parameter doing both, so the multiplier is small but cannot be 1.0. This is the second most load-bearing assumption in this file after the ROM-to-SRAM cell ratio, and it decides the storage-versus-compute-in-ROM comparison.
